Raccoonoo:

To be fair to Tempest, they were there when Captain Cosmic flew up into space with Empyreon, who visibly turned into a singularity not long afterwards. They had every reason to think Hugh was dead.

 

I'd add to this that some of the things going on might be preventing them from leaving the planet.

 

Argent Adpet is studying and protecting the Akash'Flora tree. Let's remember not only is Akash a hero who sacrificed herself by this point, but this tree in the middle of the city is all that remains of not only her, but the Void on Earth. The Nexus was destroyed, and Argent may be thinking that her connection to the void and to the planet means that this tree is vitally important.

 

And Tempest, well GLOBAL is something really intriguing here. GLOBAL is a United Nations effort, and we know Oblivaeon also targeted the Maeryinian refuge. I don't think Tempest is actually the leader of his people, but he is their public face. He's the one who has interacted the most with humans and various governments about earth. This is a political minefield potentially, and I get the feeling GLOBAL came to him. They offered the only highly public Maeryinian most people would be aware of a position on a UN team meant to deal with International and Galactic issues, including diplomacy. With the Maeryinian's being very isolated and distrusting already, Tempest declining that offer could have isolated his people even more from the global community at a time when they like everyone else is reeling from Oblivaeon and what it all meant.

 

This is all a lot of speculation, but it makes since why these two would probably take a step back and think "Void Guard and some others are heading into space to deal with a lot of stuff that Cosmic is likely to get involved in. If he's alive (which he probably isn't though I hope he is) they'll probably find him, but no one else can handle this issue here on earth. I've got to stay here and do what I can, and hope for the best."

@Raccoonoo: Ironically I think you made my point for me. There's a big difference between seeking out other people because you need help to do your job, or conversely because doing your job involves helping other people, and seeking out other people because you actually want to just be around other people.

I think AZ and Tachyon make a good contrasting example. AZ doesn't ask Tachyon to stick around and go on about her science so he can do his job or even because he's a geek himself, but at first because he's lonely and wants someone to talk to and later on because he likes having his friend talk to him.

(On the flipside I'm reminded in RL of my best friend who tended to be a loner on a personal level but liked having an audience to perform to.)

Chaosmancer:

Legacy was supposedly trapped in the rubble of Freedom Tower for the entire Oblivaeon fight, never directly participating. I feel that is completely wrong though, as we've seen artwork of Paul teaming up with his daughter and father to fight Oblivaeon, so that is an odd detail.

It would be wrong, if that's what it said, but it isn't, so it isn't.   The blurb on Legacy's starter book doesn't say he didn't participate at all, it just says he was incapacitated when Freedom Tower went down.  We don't know, that could easily have been during Oblivaeon's second (third?) form, after his little family team-up face-off.  But even that is assuming the family team-up was an actual event that happened – it may just be one of those "this is a comic cover" images that didn't really happen as shown, but is meant to metaphorically speak to Felicia taking up her father's Legacy after he gets buried under the tower's debris.

Obviously in-universe there's no reason multiple Parsons couldn't be in the same place at the same time, but the RPG blurb is adhering more closely to the game rules, where only one Legacy variant can be in play at any given time.
